items.title: FomoRobo – AI that reads your newsletters so you don't have to
items.raw_excerpt: I subscribe to dozens of newsletters and didn’t want to miss key insights, so I built an AI that reads them all and lets me ask questions about the content. I originally built it for myself, but decided to open it up in case others find it useful. Forward your newsletters to FomoRobo, and the AI will summarize the important points. Ask it questions like "What are the key facts from my newsletters today?" or "Write a blog post based on today's newsletters." The tricky part was making email parsing reliable and keeping conversation context across newsletters. It’s already processing 100+ newsletters a day. Would love feedback, especially on the UX and on what other newsletter-related pain points you would want solved. https://www.fomorobo.com Thanks!

items.title: A visual AI interface for deep research/deep dives
items.raw_excerpt: I feel like LLMs can help me understand anything. However, jumping between ChatGPT, tabs, and docs gets in the way of building real understanding beyond isolated summaries and questions. This is my attempt at fixing that — for lifelong learners, researchers, professionals and students. Would love your thoughts on the interface, and whether this would be useful in your own work or otherwise.

items.title: AI legal assistant that answers your questions with citations
items.raw_excerpt: Hi HN, I built LegesGPT, an AI legal assistant that helps speed up legal research. The problem: finding the right law or code often means digging through long government websites. It’s slow and frustrating, especially for lawyers and researchers. Our solution: you ask a legal question, and LegesGPT answers with a clear explanation plus citations from official government sites (US, UK, UAE for now). It’s already being used daily by dozens of lawyers to save hours of research. Under the hood, it uses advanced AI models reasoning + retrieval from government legal sources, so you always see where the answer came from. I’d love feedback. Whether you’re a lawyer, developer, or just curious. What features would make this more valuable to you? https://legesgpt.com

items.title: Sculptor, the Missing UI for Claude Code
items.raw_excerpt: Hey, I'm Josh, cofounder of Imbue. We built Sculptor because we wanted a great UI for parallel coding agents. We love Claude Code, but wanted to solve some of the problems that come from running multiple agents in parallel (ex: merge conflicts with multiple agents, reinstalling dependencies with git worktrees, Claude Code could deleting your home directory, etc). Sculptor is a desktop app that lets you safely run Claude Code agents by putting them in separate docker containers. This lets you use Claude without having to compromise on security or deal with annoying tool permission prompts. Then you can just tell Claude to keep running the code until it actually works. To help you easily work with containerized agents, we created “Pairing Mode”: bidirectionally sync the agent’s code into you
